name: Blue Turquoise
lede: Blue Turquoise is a light bluish green that the 1955 ISCC-NBS system traces to an older dictionary, and its archive matches are look-alikes rather than evidence of a pigment.

sections.title: A turquoise leaning blue
sections.body: The name joins [[blue-green]] ground to the gemstone color [[turquoise]]. Our sources record it in the 1930 Maerz and Paul dictionary, as cited in NBS Circular 553 of 1955 [1]. The swatch is a light bluish green, nearest ISCC-NBS name "light bluish green" at a distance of 1.7 [1]. Paterson also lists Venetian blue as a turquoise [2], so the idea of a turquoise on the blue side is an old one, but the books we read say nothing of this exact name.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch appears in 16 of our 23,781 paintings, 0.07 percent, as photographed [3]. The earliest match is dated 1508, a painting by Juan de Flandes, 422 years before the name's earliest record in our sources [3]. That is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph and not proof of any pigment or dye, and the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. Compare [[aqua]] and [[teal]] for neighbors.
